public_rationale: The non-AGI clause has direct support: Altman acknowledged missing capabilities, including continuous learning after deployment. The complete claim is broader. The documented roadmap did not promise that GPT-5 would be AGI, and the launch disclosure reports substantive improvements. The evidence does not establish the alleged overall failure against promises or the claimed leadership priority. Partial support is therefore recorded without scoring the whole claim supported.
limitations: Altman's AGI acknowledgment is established through contemporaneous reporting, not a retrieved primary briefing transcript.
OpenAI's performance figures are company-reported internal evaluations.
Useful improvements and failure to meet some promises can coexist.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Altman failed to deliver what he promised with GPT-5, and GPT-5 is in no way AGI.

statement.excerpt: Three years of hype add up, and Altman simply could not deliver what he (over)promised. GPT-5 was his primary mission as a leader, and he couldn’t get there convincingly. In no way was it AGI.

from_speaker: Altman simply could not deliver what he (over)promised
GPT-5 was his primary mission as a leader
In no way was it AGI
our_interpretation: Assess the GPT-5 system released in August 2025, not later models bearing the GPT-5 name.
The plain reading of failed delivery is a material shortfall against Altman's actual commitments, not a requirement that every promotional phrase be literally measurable.
The ordinary AGI reading requires broadly human-level general competence and adaptation, rather than strong performance on selected benchmarks.
The claim contains separate assertions about delivery, leadership priority, and AGI status. Establishing the AGI clause alone does not settle the complete claim.
A company goal of eventually developing AGI is not automatically a promise that GPT-5 would achieve it.
criteria.support_condition: The released system materially falls short of documented GPT-5 commitments, evidence establishes the claimed leadership priority, and capability evidence shows that the system did not meet the ordinary AGI reading.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The released system demonstrably meets the relevant commitments and contradicts the alleged material shortfall, credible records contradict the leadership-priority assertion, or the system demonstrably meets the ordinary AGI reading.

evidence.excerpt: we will release GPT-5 as a system
evidence.locator: Roadmap update, paragraph beginning In both ChatGPT
evidence.explanation: This is a concrete product-integration commitment. The roadmap does not commit GPT-5 to achieving AGI, so failure to achieve AGI cannot alone establish failure of this promise.

evidence.excerpt: OpenAI has yet to crack AGI.
evidence.explanation: The report describes GPT-5's launch capabilities and records Altman's explanation that it lacked continuous learning after deployment. It supports the non-AGI clause; the briefing itself occurred the preceding day.

evidence.excerpt: our best performing model on an internal benchmark
evidence.explanation: OpenAI reports improvements and expert-comparable or better results in roughly half the tested knowledge-work cases. This is relevant counterevidence to a sweeping failure characterization, but neither establishes AGI nor proves that all material promises were met.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A sufficiently complete record of GPT-5 commitments, matched launch evaluations, and evidence about the claimed leadership priority. The non-AGI clause can be assessed separately with substantially greater confidence.
